question.:question/worked-solution:
This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $25{x}^{2}=(5x)^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=5x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{5\sqrt{1-25{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5x)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\cdot (\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(5x)+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{144-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{144\cdot (1-{x}^{2}/144)}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}/144}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(x/12)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{12})}^{2}.$ 

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{12}.$ Differentiating, we get  

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{12}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=12\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{\sqrt{144-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(x/12)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot (12\,\text{d}u) \\  & =2\int \frac{\text{d}u}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}} \\  & =2\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C \\  & =2\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{x}{12})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\int \frac{7}{5\sqrt{36-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{7}{30}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}(u)+C.
$$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2 \sqrt{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{7}{5\sqrt{36-3x^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{7}{30}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{7}{30}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\cdot (2 \sqrt{3}\,\text{d}u) \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{3}}{15}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{15}+C \\ & =\frac{7 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{6} \right)}}{15}+C\end{aligned}
$$
